and so the ability to perform inductive inference seems necessary.

Universalist: In the context of an arbitrary task, an agent must map situa-
tions to responses. Such an agent could be conceived of as a progr am. A uni-
versalist approach assumes quite reasonably that for each enviro nment (or task)
there exists at least one program that always chooses the best po ssible responses

a formalisation of Ockham’s Razor named Solomonoﬀ’s Universal Prior [14,15]
which assigns a weight to every program which reconstructs what t he agent has
experienced of the environment thus far. The same model could be expressed by
programs of varying length, and so each program is evaluated by its Kolmogorov
complexity [13]; the smallest self extracting archive in a speciﬁc langua ge. This
